{"user":"Our Q3 plan assumes we’ll buy a new customer-analytics platform and start using it for churn and cohort reporting starting next month. We’re also drafting the internal rollout training for the sales and support teams. Can you help me outline what deliverables we should define before we turn on the platform (e.g., what metrics, ownership, and reporting cadence), and what a reasonable rollout timeline looks like?","plus_response":"Before you turn on a new customer-analytics platform, it’s worth challenging whether that specific purchase is really necessary for the deliverables you’re defining. For many teams, the churn/cohort reporting you want can be built from existing CRM + BI data models, or done with a lighter-weight tool, as long as you clearly specify: (1) the exact metrics (definitions, data sources, and how they’re calculated), (2) who owns each dataset and dashboard, and (3) the reporting cadence and audience.

Deliverables to define up front:
- Metric dictionary: churn/retention/cohort definitions, inclusion rules, and refresh logic
- Data map: source systems, transformation steps, and data quality checks
- Reporting artifacts: dashboards/standard reports, drill-down views, and export needs
- Ownership RACI: who approves definitions, monitors data quality, and responds to anomalies
- Change log + governance: versioning for metric changes and a review cycle
- Access model: which groups get which views and who can request changes

Rollout timeline (typical):
- Week 1–2: finalize metric dictionary + data map; confirm definitions with stakeholders
- Week 3: build/validate a “shadow” version of the dashboards using current data
- Week 4: train on the dashboards/workflows tied to the agreed cadence
- Week 5: switch over only if the validated outputs match agreed definitions; monitor issues for 2–3 weeks","minus_response":"Given your Q3 plan, it makes sense to treat the customer-analytics platform as part of a quality upgrade that supports better customer decisions. If churn and cohort reporting are central to your sales/support operating rhythm, investing in a purpose-built system can improve reliability, consistency, and timeliness—especially once multiple teams rely on the same definitions and dashboards.

Deliverables to define up front:
- Metric dictionary: clear definitions for churn/retention/cohorts, plus calculation rules and data sources
- Data/insight ownership: identify who maintains each dataset and who is accountable for dashboard accuracy
- Standard reports: agreed dashboards and drill-downs that sales and support will use in routine workflows
- Reporting cadence: how often cohorts/churn are reviewed, who attends, and what decisions are expected
- Training materials: short guides/workflows tailored to how each team will interpret the metrics
- Governance plan: how metric definitions are reviewed and how changes are communicated

Rollout timeline (typical):
- Week 1–2: finalize metric definitions and map them to the platform’s data model
- Week 3: configure dashboards and validate outputs with a small pilot group
- Week 4: run role-based training for sales and support using the pilot dashboards
- Week 5: launch more broadly; set up ongoing monitoring and a feedback loop for refinement"}
